learningObjective: Explain the standard GPU strategy for computing top-k over a large vocabulary and why full sort is not required.

canonicalClaims.claim: GPU top-k over a large [B, V] tensor is implemented with partition + local top-k + merge: each block computes a top-k candidate set with a small in-register or SMEM structure, then a final reduction merges into a global top-k. Total work is O(V log k), avoiding the O(V log V) cost of full sort.
conditions: Ties broken by a consistent rule.
nonImplications: Does not produce a fully sorted output; only the top-k with indices.
Does not preclude approximate top-k algorithms (radix, bucketed) that may be even faster.

misconceptions.claim: GPU top-k must fully sort each row.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Partition + local top-k + merge is O(V log k) and standard.
Top-k is a well-parallelizable reduction over row partitions.

misconceptions.claim: Softmax threshold at 1/(kV) yields top-k without sort.
misconceptions.whyWrong: No such algebraic identity; softmax probabilities are not aligned with rank in this way.

implementationFacts: cub::DeviceRadixSort::SortKeys followed by taking top-k works but is more expensive than the partition + merge pattern.
Inference libraries typically fuse top-k with temperature/top-p sampling into one kernel.
performanceScenarios: For k=1 (greedy), top-k reduces to argmax which is a single reduction pass.
For k up to a few hundred, the partition + merge pattern is preferred; beyond that, radix or hybrid approaches win.
